chunks: And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:
Be patient with the enemies of blessings, for you cannot repay one who disobeys Allah concerning you with anything better than obeying Allah concerning him.

key_terms.أَعْدَاءِ ٱلنِّعَمِ: those who resent, oppose, or envy the blessings granted to someone
key_terms.تُطِيعَ ٱللَّهَ: to obey Allah in one's conduct

ai.seo_question: How should a believer respond to people who envy their blessings or wrong them?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches restraint and moral excellence in dealing with those who resent or oppose the blessings one has received. The best response to someone's sinful conduct toward you is not retaliation in kind, but obedience to Allah in how you treat them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5852 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), peace be upon him, who said:
"Be patient with those who are envious of your blessings, for you cannot repay one who disobeys Allah (swt) regarding you with anything better than obeying Allah (swt) concerning him."
